Front: readString/readAllLines vs BufferedReader/Files.lines(), and why does Files.lines() need try-with-resources?
Back: readString() and readAllLines() load the whole file into memory: fine for small files. BufferedReader and Files.lines() process line by line, which suits large files. Files.lines() returns a lazy Stream<String> backed by an open file handle, so it must be closed: `try (Stream<String> lines = Files.lines(path)) { ... }`. Try-with-resources closes any AutoCloseable even when an exception is thrown.

Front: Why not use MultipartFile.getOriginalFilename() as the storage path, and how do you store an upload safely?
Back: The client controls the name, so "../../important-file.txt" enables path traversal. Store under a generated name (UUID + ".bin") and keep the original name only as metadata. Resolve against a fixed root and verify: `target = root.resolve(name).normalize(); if (!target.startsWith(root)) throw ...`. Copy with `Files.copy(file.getInputStream(), target)`, not getBytes(), which loads the whole upload into memory. Limit size with spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size.

Front: Why might an @ExceptionHandler for FileNotFoundException never produce your 404?
Back: (1) The parameter type must match: `handleFileNotFound(IllegalArgumentException ex, ...)` mapped to FileNotFoundException fails with "Could not resolve parameter [0]" and the request becomes a 500. (2) Files.* (NIO) throws java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException, which isn't a FileNotFoundException. (3) Wrapped exceptions such as RuntimeException(cause) are matched by cause, but cleaner to throw a domain exception (e.g. StoredFileNotFoundException) and map that to 404.
